Build the derived-column tables

Source: R/md-derive.R
md_build_derived.Rd

Runs npmatch::np_normalize() over name and address and stores the output as name_derived and address_derived, keyed on name_id / address_id.

Usage

md_build_derived(
  con = NULL,
  what = c("name", "address"),
  chunk = 1000000L,
  incremental = FALSE
)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

what

Which tables to build.

chunk

Rows per pass. Bounds peak memory, not correctness.

incremental

Derive only rows that have no derived row yet, and delete derived rows whose source row is gone. For adding a source to a built database; refused if the stored rows were built by another normalizer.

Value

Row counts, invisibly.

Why separate tables rather than columns

§9 says the normalizer will drift, and it already has once. When it does, the derived values are stale and the base rows are not. Separate tables make that a DROP and a rebuild rather than an ALTER rewriting 18.5M rows in tables that are meant to be append-only, and they let the signature be checked per table: a mismatch says exactly which artifact to rebuild.

Why it costs what it costs

np_normalize() computes all 19 derived columns regardless of input, so the name pass also parses streets over stub columns and the address pass parses names it will not keep. Measured at 18.1 s and 14.0 s per 200,000 rows, which is roughly 36 minutes for both tables and about half of that wasted. The waste is accepted deliberately: calling the exported function is what makes np_normalize_signature() a true statement about how these columns were produced. Calling internals would be faster and would make the stamp a lie.
